<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="one-tree-several-hosts"><a href="#one-tree-several-hosts">One tree, several hosts</a></h2>

The Gama README describes a modular declarative UI framework written in Swift. A retained render tree connects application state and views to layout, drawing, and platform integrations.

The documented integrations include terminal, Apple, WebAssembly, C/Android, MLIR, and Embedded Swift surfaces. That list describes the project’s architecture; it is not a statement that this review ran every platform acceptance test.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="modules-with-clear-jobs"><a href="#modules-with-clear-jobs">Modules with clear jobs</a></h2>

GamaCore contains scene, view, identity, state, layout, event, and FrameHost concepts. GamaTUI supplies a terminal backend, while GamaAppleUI provides an Apple host view. GamaWASM, GamaEmbed, and GamaMLIR cover other integration boundaries.

The README describes an explicit primary scene with optional auxiliary surfaces. Read its current migration notes before applying an older application example; a declarative API can change between project revisions.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="verify-your-target"><a href="#verify-your-target">Verify your target</a></h2>

Choose the host you need, read the actual module instructions, and run the relevant acceptance flow with the supported toolchain. Do not substitute a generic cross-platform claim for evidence on your target.

No installation command or language-version requirement is invented here. The upstream source is authoritative for setup. Keep measurements attached to their environment rather than treating a measurement harness as a performance guarantee.

</section>
